craft_notes: Sthāyin: wonder at measurability (the infinite fingered). Sanskrit first: two measures triangulating a midpoint, then two traditional names → L4 sets measures line 1, names line 2 (colon landing on tradition). Rows: row 3 (correlative balance — five/two, navel/root). Rupture: dash after 'root' — measuring done, beholding starts. Close: colon-to-period ('remembered ground' — the ground remembers). Minimal pass: 'root' for 'member' (plain, singable, same body). Read aloud: numbers tick (five, two), dash hush, line 2 settles low. Rejected: 'organ'/'member' kept literal — killed: singability is music's office, doctrine untouched; splitting measures across the break — killed: easing what Sanskrit packs.

lines: Five fingers down from the navel, two above the root —
between them the Bulb: the wheel's remembered ground.
l4.sanskrit_cite: nābhyadho 'ṅgulāḥ pañca meḍhrasyordhvāṅguladvayam / tanmadhye kandanāmā ca cakrasthānamiti smṛtam

reads_against.argmap: The standing place is a measurable bodily site with two traditional names.
c1_essence: The bulb's site measured: five below the navel, two above — the wheel's station.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with vīra-utsāha (wonder braced by resolve)
